disposition_reason: Total mercury in canned mussels, squid, oysters, clams and octopus bought in Mazatlán supermarkets, on dry and wet weight basis.

study.design: retail survey of canned mollusks (one product per mollusk type)
study.origin: oysters and clams canned in Mexico; octopus, mussels and squid imported from the USA, South Korea and Spain
study.method: drained, lyophilized; HNO3 hot-plate digestion; total Hg by cold vapor AAS (Buck 410)
study.qa: NIST 2976 mussel tissue CRM, recovery 98.7 ± 3.1%; blanks every 20 samples

material.label_as_printed: Canned mussels, smoked in vegetable oil

findings.group: retail product A, imported from South Korea, Mazatlán supermarkets
findings.notes: 10 cans of one product, each can drained and half the contents taken as a sample; bought January 2014 in supermarkets in Mazatlán; lyophilized; CV-AAS; SD exceeds the mean

unresolved: MeHg values in Table 2 are estimated from assumed MeHg:Hg ratios (0.3915 bivalves, 0.81 octopus, 0.92 squid); not recorded as findings.
Text states wet-weight Hg of 0.003-0.007 mg/kg and calls 0.003 mg/kg the mussel value, but Table 2 prints 0.0013-0.0040 mg/kg wet weight (mussels 0.0013).
Each mollusk type is a single brand/product (10 cans); results do not represent the category broadly.
